headlines: Relief Collection Exposed as a Private Purse
False Charity Jar Brings Public Reckoning
bodies: {A} collected money for a relief fund that did not exist. After the Gazette checked the appeal, the collector returned the donations and paid additional costs from personal funds.
A relief jar organized by {A} proved to have no fund behind it. Public exposure forced repayment, leaving the collector poorer and facing widespread distrust.
The Gazette found that a charitable appeal promoted by {A} was invented. The money was repaid at personal expense after donors demanded an accounting.

headlines: Receipts Clear Relief Organizer of Suspicion
Relief Fund Books Answer a Town's Questions
{A.last} Opens Donation Ledger to Public View
bodies: Questions about a relief collection led {A} to make its receipts available for inspection. Every donation was accounted for, and the Gazette found no money diverted.
{A} answered suspicions about a relief jar by opening the collection ledger. Receipts confirmed that the full amount reached the intended aid fund.
A disputed relief appeal organized by {A} passed a public accounting. The Gazette inspected the receipts and found the accusations unsupported.

items.era_notes: Use paper ledgers and receipts throughout; name no outside charity or disaster. The simulation selects whether this appeal is fraudulent or legitimate.

headlines: A Scarecrow Wears Its Maker's Sense of Humor
Parent and Child Give Straw a Personality
bodies: {A} and parent {B} entered a scarecrow with enormous stuffed ears in the town's autumn display. The card beneath it read 'Good Listener,' and visitors supplied plenty of conversation.
An autumn scarecrow built by {A} with help from parent {B} drew delighted attention. Its outsized ears and 'Good Listener' label earned the young maker public praise.
{A} handled the design and parent {B} handled the knots for a scarecrow in the autumn display. Their big-eared creation became a favorite place for visitors to pose and laugh.

headlines: Scarecrow Entry Becomes a Family Dispute
Young Maker Objects as Parent Claims the Credit
Autumn Display Reveals More Than Straw
bodies: {B} claimed sole credit for a scarecrow designed and built mostly by child {A}. After {A} objected in front of visitors, the display became the setting for an uncomfortable family argument.
A scarecrow in the autumn display brought {A} little pleasure after parent {B} dismissed the child's work as mere watching. Visitors heard a correction from the young maker.
{A} challenged parent {B} for taking credit for a scarecrow that was largely the child's work. The resulting argument drew more notice than the entry itself.

items.era_notes: Keep this a local autumn display rather than a branded or regional festival. B is A's parent; photographs are optional and absent from the base text.

items.text: They say {A} has been measuring the shadow of a fence belonging to {B} to prove it steals afternoon sunshine.
variants: I hear {A} is measuring the shade from the fence belonging to {B}; I hope they can talk before the ruler becomes evidence.
{A} supposedly measures the shade cast by the fence belonging to {B}.
Has {A} accounted for the sun moving, or is that going on the complaint against {B} too?

items.text: I hear {A} keeps a jar of polished stones ready for children who arrive with nothing to trade.
variants: They say {A} makes sure every child has a stone worth trading; small kindnesses can fill a pocket.
{A} supposedly gives trading stones to children who have none.
How does {A} decide which stones are valuable, and why does everybody seem to want the plain striped ones?

items.text: Word is {A} used a borrowed fishing rod from {B} to prop open a window and snapped it.
variants: I hope {A} offers to replace that rod from {B}; borrowed things deserve better than a window frame.
They say {A} broke a rod borrowed from {B} by using it as a window prop.
Did {A} mention the window when returning the rod to {B}, or only complain that the fishing had been poor?

items.text: People say {A} and {B} have agreed to share one sled by counting downhill turns and uphill pulls separately.
variants: I hear {A} and {B} found a fair way to share a sled; they even count the work of hauling it back.
{A} and {B} supposedly keep separate counts for sled rides and pulls.
Who audits the sled accounts for {A} and {B} when somebody claims the hill was shorter last time?

items.text: They say {A} found a fresh wet footprint on the underside of a porch step.
variants: I hear {A} found a footprint under a step; perhaps someone moved the board after it was marked.
{A} supposedly found a wet footprint beneath a porch stair.
If that print was really underneath the step, did {A} check whether it was pointing into the house or out?

Come back when you have a little time to spare.
I had better get on. It was good talking with you.
May the rest of your day be an easy one.
We will have something new to discuss next time.
You know where to find me. Stop and say hello.

I have kept you long enough.
I will leave you to it.
